topic: Christensen-Burley dual-exponential BSSRDF vs Gaussian wax blur rig
topic_zh: Christensen-Burley 双指数次表面散射扩散剖面对比朴素单高斯塑料蜡感
scope: Deterministic Per Christensen & Brent Burley (Pixar SIGGRAPH 2015 / RenderMan / Blender Principled BSSRDF) dual-exponential radial diffusion profile (I_CB(u) = 0.5*(exp(-u) + exp(-u/3)) for normalized scatter radius u = r/d in [0.00, 4.00]) versus naive single-Gaussian blur (exp(-u^2/2)) and 64-dipole multipole quadrature across 17 radial stations.

protocol.function: I_CB(u) = ½·(e^(−u) + e^(−u/3)) → r=3d Tail = 0.2088 vs Single-Gaussian 0.0111 (−94.68% Tail Extinction)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 radial mean-free-path stations preserve both the sharp single-scatter cusp and deep translucent tail

good_fit: Jade, marble statues, wax candles, milk, and human skin in Pixar RenderMan, Blender Cycles/EEVEE, and UE5 Subsurface Profile
Combining a sharp near-source cusp (e^(-r/d)) for crisp pores with a wide diffusion tail (e^(-r/3d)) for deep translucency
Eliminating the +11.86% near-core wax bloat at 1d and -94.68% deep-tail extinction at 3d of single-Gaussian blurs
Direct importance sampling via analytic CDF inversion in 2 exponential terms without dipole Hankel integrals
not_for: Opaque metallic conductors with zero subsurface penetration (use Gulbrandsen Conductor Fresnel Round 107)
Optically thin single-sheet foliage without multiple internal scattering
Large-scale atmospheric sky Rayleigh/Mie airmass (use Spherical Atmosphere Round 73)
